clue.text: Man is able to become religious

definitions.note: a noun here: a member of a religious order

parts.note: Francis is a man's first name
is able means can

explanation.surface: A man finds himself capable of turning to faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' is used as a noun, a monk or friar, as in 'the religious of the abbey'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Franciscan is a friar of the order founded by St Francis of Assisi, so a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Time for an accident

definitions.meaning: the American word for the season of autumn
a tumble, such as one on ice

explanation.definitionFit: The season after summer is called this in America, and a trip to the ground is also called this.

clue.text: Approaches and performs without society's backing

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: performs means acts

indicators.note: backing says the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: Soc is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: He takes the stage without support from the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside', the container; 'backing' turns the society abbreviation round to COS.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to go up and speak to them, often boldly, so it means approaches.

clue.text: Vessel which may make no East China trips

indicators.note: make, in the sense of form into something, has the letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: A ship that never sails to the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges NO, E and CHINA TRIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A container ship is a cargo vessel built to carry goods packed in standard boxes.

clue.text: Divisions or other parts of army

definitions.meaning: pieces or segments that something is cut into
in the army a small unit within a platoon has this name

explanation.definitionFit: Segments of anything are called this, and so are the small units into which an army platoon is split.

clue.text: A bachelor seer, in something dirty is put to shame

parts.note: ash is the dirty residue left by a fire

explanation.surface: An unmarried man is caught in a grubby state and feels humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seer' gives nothing; it is almost certainly a misprint for 'seen', which links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to embarrass or disconcert them, making them feel ashamed.

clue.text: Inch which may cover a large area

definitions.text: Inch which may cover a large area

parts.words: Inch which may cover a large area
parts.note: inch is the Scottish word for a small island, and an island of that kind can be anything from a rock to a landmass, so this 'inch' may be huge

explanation.walkthrough: An inch is a Scottish island (Inchcolm, Inchmurrin); the surface plays on the inch as the tiny unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an inch is a small island, and an island of any size is a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: It stops a leak when there is a boy in the class

indicators.note: in places the boy's name inside the word for a class

parts.note: a set is a class or group of pupils
Alan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Plugging a drip by putting a schoolboy in the right form.
explanation.walkthrough: A set is a teaching group of pupils of similar ability, as in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a substance applied to close gaps and keep water or air from getting through.

clue.text: Expansive people in a branch of medicine show expression of affection

indicators.note: in puts the costly people inside the medical branch

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
read as expensive, which means dear
people means men

explanation.surface: Costly staff in a hospital department show warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expansive' is almost certainly a misprint for 'expensive', which means DEAR; ENT is the hospital's ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.definitionFit: An endearment is a fond word such as 'darling', so a loving phrase.

clue.text: Classical poet put back in the vernacular

indicators.note: put back tells us to read the run of letters backwards
in says the letters sit inside the word vernacular

explanation.surface: An ancient poet has been rendered back into everyday speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to NACUL inside 'vernacular', and 'put back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucan was a Roman poet of the first century AD who wrote the epic Pharsalia, so a classical writer of verse.

clue.text: Applaud directors for covering of house

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
a company's directors make up its board

explanation.surface: Clapping the board members over a matter of house cladding.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapboard is overlapping timber siding fixed to the outside walls of a building.

clue.text: Be paid a shilling for gas as a transient visitor

indicators.note: as a transient, in a passing and shifting form, has the letters move about

parts.note: s was the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money

explanation.surface: Being handed a shilling to feed the gas meter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transient' rearranges BE PAID, S and FOR GAS. Gas meters in British homes once took shilling coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of passage is someone who stays only briefly before moving on, like a migrating bird.

clue.text: In a lot of boats the bridge exists to injure a girl

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
exists means is
to injure is to harm
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a crowded harbour, a bridge is a menace to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish Armada was the fleet Philip II sent against England in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada was a huge fleet of warships, so it was very many vessels at once.

clue.text: Pursues being clever in school tasks

indicators.note: in has the word for clever placed inside the school exercises

parts.note: proses are translation exercises set at school
cute can mean clever or shrewd

explanation.surface: A bright pupil gets on with homework.
explanation.walkthrough: A prose is a passage for translation into a foreign language, a standard British school exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute a plan or a case is to carry it on or follow it through.

clue.text: Ringing when a woman enters the wrong store

indicators.note: enters means the woman's name goes inside the other letters
wrong suggests the letters of store are set out in a wrong order

parts.note: Nan is a woman's name, short for Ann

explanation.surface: A woman walks into the wrong shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' shuffles the letters of 'store' to RESOT; 'enters' is the container signal, and 'Ringing' is an adjective here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is a full, echoing one that keeps ringing on.

clue.text: Instrument for two cats

indicators.note: two calls for the word for a cat to appear twice over

parts.note: a tom is a male cat; the clue's two cats give it twice

explanation.surface: A musical instrument meant to be shared by a pair of cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a tall drum played with the hands, so a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Drive the past away when penalties are taken

annotationWithheld.why: Drive the past away when penalties are taken: SHOOT (drive) + OUT (away) leaves 'the past' with no job; likely an OCR or setting slip, no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Drive the past away when penalties are taken

clue.text: Ridicule makes a country grow weary

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
to grow weary is to tire

explanation.surface: Mockery so relentless that a whole nation gets fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is mockery of folly or vice through irony and exaggeration.

clue.text: Call a little bit up for the cart

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the whole run is read from the bottom

parts.note: to call out is to yell
an ort is a scrap of food left over

explanation.surface: Shout a little to fetch the trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns YELLORT round. ORT is an old word for a scrap of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolley is a small wheeled vehicle pushed by hand, a kind of handcart.

clue.text: Protector gives drink to former head of state

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
Juan Perón was president of Argentina

explanation.surface: A bodyguard pours a cup for an old dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is old British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon looks after a young person, especially a young woman, in company, so a guardian.

clue.text: Artists with a woman's food

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, so RAs are artists
something belonging to a woman is hers

explanation.surface: Painters share a woman's meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers are slices of bacon, a breakfast staple.

clue.text: Finishes without the endless stretch of coastline appearing in the frames

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the others

parts.note: finishes means closes

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a shore is a stretch of coast

explanation.surface: Picture-frame work is finished without a long coastal view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside', so the word for finishes goes round the rest; 'endless' drops the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes horses are folding wooden racks on which laundry is hung to dry.

clue.text: Opening created by splitting atoms

indicators.note: splitting breaks the word atoms apart so its letters re-form

explanation.surface: A gap made by nuclear fission.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoma is a small pore in a leaf or a surgical hole in the body.

clue.text: Supplies an extra tool, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for a tool is to be heard, not seen

parts.note: an adze is a woodworking tool with an arched blade

explanation.surface: The workshop orders one more cutting implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Adds means puts in more, so it gives something additional.

clue.text: Turning to the pole for distant shots

indicators.note: turning tells us the letters of the next three words are moved round

explanation.surface: Swinging round to point at the pole to take far-off pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens magnifies far-off subjects, so it is used to photograph things a long way off.

clue.text: People discovered in time to make an improvement

indicators.note: in places the word for people inside the time letters

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the years of our time
people means men

explanation.surface: Men found just in time to put things right.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to change something for the better, by correction or revision.

clue.text: Speaks for youth being held by military men

indicators.note: being held by means the letter goes inside the soldiers' abbreviation

parts.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, is a British army regiment
Y is the abbreviation for youth, as in YMCA

explanation.surface: Soldiers have a young recruit in their grip who talks on his behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Says means utters or talks, the verb in the third person as speaks is.

clue.text: If they had no hair in them these beds would do for couples

definitions.text: If they had no hair in them these beds would do for couples

parts.words: If they had no hair in them these beds would do for couples
parts.note: take the word for locks of hair out of the word for these beds, and what is left is a word for partners

explanation.walkthrough: Remove TRESS (a lock of hair) from the answer and MATES (couples, partners) remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Mattresses are the padded parts of beds that people sleep on.
